clue.text: Chow said to need time for dog mess, but no pees!

indicators.note: having no pees means every letter P is struck out of the dog and its mess

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a breed of dog
the mess a dog leaves behind

explanation.surface: Someone frets that their dog's mess needs time to clear, with an exclamation about the absence of wee.
explanation.walkthrough: Chow said is ciao spoken aloud, the Italian goodbye. The mess is the dog's own, and every letter P must go from both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-oo is a jaunty British farewell, just as ciao is an Italian way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Sound of cat, or sound of donkey

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, so what follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a mule is a donkey crossed with a horse

explanation.surface: Someone tries to tell a cat's cry apart from a donkey's.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves begin 'sound of', but only the second is the signal: the donkey gives a word pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mewl is to whimper feebly, the thin plaintive cry a kitten or cat makes.

clue.text: Cleaner pack of lies

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a paper hankie used for wiping
second meaning: a web of falsehoods, as in the phrase 'a ___ of lies'

explanation.surface: An accusation that the cleaner's story is entirely invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' reads as a person, but it is the paper you clean with.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft paper wipe is a cleaner, and an elaborate interwoven set of falsehoods is called a tissue of lies.

clue.text: Paul in France for nearly a month? I'm not sure I should (bit of a gut)

indicators.note: nearly the whole thing means stopping one letter short of its end

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so he is 'I', which in French is je
the sixth month
the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: The setter wonders whether to spend most of a month in France, with a nervous gut.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves by name, so 'Paul' means 'I', here translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: The jejunum is the middle section of the small intestine, so it is one part of the gut.

clue.text: Opposing sides to gather praise when moving counter

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in, so the sides close around the rest

parts.note: right and left, the two opposite sides

indicators.note: letters that are moving do not stay in their printed order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rival teams applaud a player making a counter-attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a verb but is a noun: a counter-strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation, a hit back against an attack, which is a counter.

clue.text: Stupid person expecting to stand for the fare

parts.note: dumb means stupid
one who waits for something to happen

explanation.surface: A dim passenger expects to stand while paying the fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' reads as a ticket price but means food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a serving trolley or small lift on which dishes of food are set out, a stand for meals.

clue.text: "I'm a lumberjack", though my gender is under discussion

indicators.note: being discussed means being talked about out loud, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: the speaker is a lumberjack, a man, and a fella is a casual word for one

explanation.surface: The Monty Python lumberjack, who likes dressing in women's clothes, finds his gender questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Monty Python song has a lumberjack who wears women's clothing, so his gender is indeed debatable.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberjack cuts down trees, and one who fells timber is a feller.

clue.text: Hickey's obit (end of life)

parts.note: read as O then BIT, with the O being love, the tennis score of zero, written out in full

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of life

explanation.surface: A newspaper obituary for someone named Hickey, marking his death.
explanation.walkthrough: Split obit into O and BIT, swap the O for the word it stands for in tennis, love, and add E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hickey is the American word for a love bite, the bruise left by a passionate kiss.

clue.text: Bring forth English dictator

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Il Duce was the title of the Italian dictator Mussolini

explanation.surface: A command to produce an English tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or elicit something latent, which is to bring it forth.

clue.text: Percentage-wise, you must do as much as me, darling

parts.words: you must do as much as me
parts.note: the vow 'I do' that each partner says in turn at a wedding
L is the Roman numeral fifty, an equal half share as a percentage

explanation.surface: A partner demands a fair half-and-half split of the chores.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'I do fifty': doing as much as me means each does fifty per cent.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is a much-loved favourite, and an idol is someone adored and admired in the same way.

clue.text: A pass that's impossible to roll?

definitions.text: A pass that's impossible to roll?

parts.words: A pass that's impossible to roll?
parts.note: surface: a mysterious delivery that cannot travel along the ground
setter's reading: a thing with corners rather than a round shape could never roll

explanation.walkthrough: In football a square ball is a pass straight across the pitch; read literally, a cube-shaped ball would never roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A square ball is the football term for a sideways pass across the field, often a risky one.

clue.text: Church shows a weakness in the head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a building for worship
second meaning: the thin-boned flat area at the side of the skull

explanation.surface: A church reveals a failing in its leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a place of worship, and the temple is the fragile part of the skull between eye and ear.

clue.text: One penny piece passed round, broken, for instance

indicators.note: something passed round another wraps it on either side

parts.note: a tiny piece of something
Roman numeral one
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A single coin was handed around and ended up damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' looks like describing the coin, but the definition is grammatical: broken is an example of a past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: A participle is a verb form used as an adjective, and broken is the past form of break.

clue.text: Reported higher flaw in the mind

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by voice, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: ups for higher things, and tears in the sense of rips, which are flaws

explanation.surface: A news story about an upper-level defect in someone's thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Tears here are rips, said to rhyme with 'wears'. 'Not much upstairs' is the idiom behind the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstairs is informal for the head or brain, as in having nothing upstairs, meaning in one's mind.

clue.text: Blimey vicar, there's no alternative? That's right!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: there being none of something means it is taken away

parts.note: a parish clergyman
or is the word that offers an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a vicar who insists there is no other option.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and right both mean accurate or true, used as an exclamation of agreement.

clue.text: Cab to hire on ring road

parts.note: to call a taxi is to hire one
O is ring-shaped
a way is a road

explanation.surface: Instructions for hailing a taxi on a ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: Cab is not a taxi but a first name: the jazz bandleader Cab Calloway.
explanation.definitionFit: Cab Calloway was the American jazz singer and bandleader famous for Minnie the Moocher.

clue.text: Some time in prison for informant?
Composition with a fruity twist?

parts.note: a citrus fruit
to rick is to wrench or sprain a joint

explanation.surface: A drink or recipe given a zest of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Limericks are known for twist endings and fruity, saucy humour, so the clue reads both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick is a short comic five-line poem, which is a piece of written composition.

clue.text: Suspicion doesn't begin about murder, but divorce

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
failing to begin means the opening letter is lost

parts.note: a hunch is a suspicion
a hit is a contract killing

explanation.surface: A suspicious spouse who stops short of murder settles for divorce instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch is to uncouple or separate two things, and to divorce means to part or detach.

clue.text: Nick holding pad, non-starter for bellringing

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside

parts.note: both are British slang for prison

indicators.note: a non-starter has no first part, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: a Brillo pad is a brand of scouring pad

explanation.surface: Someone named Nick keeps a notepad for jotting down bellringing changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick reads as a man's name but is slang for jail, as is can. The pad that loses its first letter is the scouring kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of bells in a tower played from a keyboard, so it is used for bellringing.

clue.text: Father in pain must be brave

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: an ache is a pain
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father suffering must keep a stiff upper lip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is not an adjective here but a noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Apache are a Native American people known for their warriors.

clue.text: Be economical with small wave

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to crimp hair is to give it small waves

explanation.surface: Advice to be frugal and wave only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to save money by spending as little as possible, which is being thrifty.

clue.text: Lager girl, losing head, hammers the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means reading back to front
losing the head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: mallets are wooden hammers

explanation.surface: A girl drinking lager loses her head and starts swinging hammers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition does double duty: a brand of lager and a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella Artois is a well-known Belgian lager, and Stella is also a girl's first name.

clue.text: Turn into one place, which overlooks Rome

indicators.note: to turn things is to rearrange them out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn into a vantage point looking out over Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capitoline is one of the seven hills of Rome, rising above the Forum and the city centre.

clue.text: See 17
Invention is kind of grand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one's own pet project or creation
second meaning: the smaller type of grand piano

explanation.surface: A claim that some invention is rather impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' reads as an adjective meaning splendid, but it is the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A project someone created is called their baby, and a baby grand is a compact grand piano.

clue.text: Board game won by lethal mastery

indicators.note: something won by another is held in its possession, so it sits inside those words

parts.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A board game victory achieved through ruthless skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a Victorian strategy game played by jumping pieces across a checkered board, a forerunner of Chinese chequers.

clue.text: With which there's no riding of a bicycle

definitions.text: With which there's no riding of a bicycle

indicators.note: riding tumbles and jolts the following letters out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rule banning cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: riding is slang for sex, which celibacy rules out.
explanation.definitionFit: Celibacy is abstaining from sexual relations, so there is none of the riding in the vulgar sense.
